central_question: Does the evidence available after the failed V10 mechanism gate justify another bounded FP-NAA performance hypothesis, and which candidate mechanisms remain distinct, leakage-controlled, and falsifiable?
contribution_statement: The post-V10 literature gate rejects threshold-only tail rescue, another correlated BEATs score union, and proxy-fault model selection as immediate successors; it retains cross-channel predictive residuals and domain-aware calibration only as prior-art comparators inside a new safety or transfer study, not as novel components by themselves.

prohibited_claims.evidence_scope: The aggregation family is already described and its reported development replay does not favor it over consensus.
prohibited_claims.text: Do not present sparse top-tail rescue or a relaxed median-gain rule as a novel V11 mechanism.

prohibited_claims.evidence_scope: A direct DCASE 2026 system description implements this mechanism with normal-only ridge prediction.
prohibited_claims.text: Do not claim that predicting one channel representation from the other and scoring the residual is itself novel.

prohibited_claims.evidence_scope: Direct transfer analysis and strict leave-one-machine-out validation practice.
prohibited_claims.text: Do not use development-score ranking alone as evidence that a configuration will transfer to unseen evaluation machine types.

prohibited_claims.evidence_scope: Proxy outliers saturate competing backends in the reported ASD study and fail to provide a useful selection signal.
prohibited_claims.text: Do not claim that passing a synthetic or proxy-fault gate proves ranking power on real anomalies.

prohibited_claims.evidence_scope: Multiple current primary system descriptions already cover these aggregation families.
prohibited_claims.text: Do not claim generic score calibration, rank fusion, maximum fusion, or multi-branch ensembling as a CARE-ASD novelty.

prohibited_claims.evidence_scope: The official challenge publication policy distinguishes technical reports from reviewed workshop papers.
prohibited_claims.text: Do not describe DCASE challenge technical reports in this delta as peer-reviewed scientific evidence.

supported_claims.evidence_scope: Direct ASD systematic evidence and current challenge system descriptions; not a universal theorem over every encoder or dataset.
supported_claims.text: For the next bounded study, backend and representation diversity deserves priority over another temporal-pooling or same-representation branch search.

supported_claims.evidence_scope: A direct negative ASD result plus evidence that label-free criteria need an independent viability check.
supported_claims.text: Pseudo-fault or proxy-outlier selection cannot by itself authorize a performance run because proxy discrimination may fail to rank real-anomaly backends.

supported_claims.evidence_scope: Cross-year ASD experiments with an explicitly disclosed degenerate-map failure mode.
supported_claims.text: Domain-aware normal-score calibration is a necessary transfer control, but normal-distribution balance does not certify anomaly-detection power and requires a frozen viability veto.

supported_claims.evidence_scope: Current DCASE technical reports demonstrate the component families but do not report CARE-ASD's known-component preservation endpoints.
supported_claims.text: Cross-channel predictive residuals remain mechanistically distinct from the failed V10 score branches, but only a new safety, identifiability, or transfer protocol could be a CARE-ASD contribution.

supported_claims.evidence_scope: A go-or-no-go research-program decision combining current prior art with the already frozen CARE-ASD V10 failure.
supported_claims.text: The literature delta does not justify immediate V11 GPU training; a successor must first state a mechanism not reducible to tail-threshold tuning, ordinary fusion, or reconstruction of a published ensemble.

working_title: Post-V10 Literature Gate for CARE-ASD Successor Research
